thesis: KXNFLFANTASYMOST is a per-game, mutually-exclusive 'which player has the most fantasy points in this game' contract governed by the generic RANKLIST rulebook (contract_terms_url confirmed live: https://assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/NFLFANTASY.pdf, text verbatim-identical to RANKLIST.pdf), which pays an exact-tie $1/n pro-rata split (rounded down) rather than $0 to the loser, structurally the same mechanism validated as a green-light edge in P-022 golf round-leader markets. IF (a) Kalshi relists this product on a recurring weekly cadence during the 2026 season and (b) exact point ties occur at a non-trivial rate given ESPN's fractional PPR scoring precision, THEN retail market pricing on the top 1-2 favorites (who price as if a single clean winner exists) should be measurably too high versus a tie-adjusted fair value, net of the taker fee and half-spread. This is NOT yet established fact — it is a candidate hypothesis pending live-market observation. This is a genuinely different product from the killed op_20260801_001 (KXRANKLISTFF*, season-long #1-only fantasy rank), and is falsifiable independently: it fails if the product does not recur beyond its one observed instance, or if the empirical tie rate at ESPN's scoring precision is small enough that $1/n haircut on any single favorite is sub-tick ($0.01).
edge_source: RANKLIST template's conditional $1/n dead-heat clause (verbatim, read directly from the live NFLFANTASY.pdf, not inferred from the ticker name) pays exact ties pro-rata rather than $0 -- if retail order flow prices the market-favorite candidate as if an outright win is the only tie-free outcome, the favorite's YES price should be structurally too high by the tie-mass haircut, mirroring P-022's validated golf round-leader mechanism (per manager/registry.yaml / MEMORY.md: 'P-022 fade Phase-2 GREEN-LIGHT ... survives adverse selection, +2-5c/ct, small capacity, caps required').

Series is fee-classified 'quadratic' (maker-free) both live (GET /series/KXNFLFANTASYMOST -> fee_type: 'quadratic') and in the generated fixture (src/fixtures/kalshi_series_fees.json: KXNFLFANTASYMOST present in all_series, ABSENT from maker_fee_series -> series_maker_charges_fee() returns False), consistent with CLAUDE.md's documented finding that 'Leader markets are maker-free -- all of them' -- a maker-side entry here would carry zero maker fee, same cost-basis regime golf P-022 exploited.

Single-game fantasy-point totals should show materially higher exact-tie mass than season-long totals (the KXRANKLISTFF* premise this scout was sent to re-examine), because fewer scoring events accumulate before the tie window closes -- shrinking, not eliminating, the precision problem noted below under failure modes.
external_data_needed: Player-level, per-game fantasy-point distributions at ESPN's exact scoring precision (standard ESPN default PPR uses hundredths, e.g. 0.04 pts/yard) -- needed to empirically estimate exact-tie probability among the top-2/top-3 candidates in a typical game; not present anywhere in this repo (no nflfastR / box-score ingestion module exists).

Confirmation that Kalshi actually relists KXNFLFANTASYMOST for 2026 regular-season games once the season starts in September -- the series currently shows exactly ONE event in its entire history (KXNFLFANTASYMOST-26FEB08SEANE, Super Bowl LX, already settled and purged) and zero events for any prior or upcoming regular-season game. Cadence is unverified in either direction and must be monitored, not assumed.

A live/near-settlement instance of this specific series to inspect result / settlement_value_dollars behavior firsthand -- the one historical event's markets array is already empty (fully purged, matching the documented Kalshi purge-after-settlement pattern in satellites_research/REPORT_Satellites_2026-07.md), so the scalar-tie-payout mechanism, while governed on paper by the RANKLIST text, has never been observed settling for THIS series.

ESPN Fantasy's own published methodology (or confirmation none exists) for how it would break a tie in game-level fantasy scoring -- WebFetch could not reach espn.com/fantasy pages in the prior integrity review (404/403/JS-rendered), so whether the RANKLIST clause's 'if none exists' precondition is even satisfied for this product remains unconfirmed; treated in this card as PLAUSIBLE (a single-game leaderboard is not something ESPN formally publishes with an official tiebreak procedure, unlike season awards) but not verified.

The candidate universe construction rule for a given game (does Kalshi list a market for every player who appears in the box score, only starters, or only 'reasonably live' skill-position players?) -- unobservable from the purged event and must be captured the next time this series has open markets.
known_failure_modes: Cadence collapse: the series has exactly one event in its entire observed history (the just-completed Super Bowl) and zero regular-season instances. If Kalshi treats KXNFLFANTASYMOST as a marquee-game-only special (Super Bowl, maybe conference championships) rather than a weekly product, capacity is at most a handful of events per year -- not enough for a viable pod, and not enough to backtest a tie-rate estimate with any statistical power (n=1 today, contrast with P-022's dozens of golf tournaments).

Sub-tick edge: PPR fantasy scoring is fractional to the hundredth of a point (yardage bonuses etc.), unlike golf strokes (integer) or round-leader ties (CLAUDE.md's documented 9.4% H2H tie rate). Exact ties to hundredths-of-a-point precision in a single game may be rare enough that the $1/n haircut on any single favorite is smaller than the $0.01 minimum tick -- CLAUDE.md explicitly notes 'the repo has killed several structural-tie ideas that were real but smaller than one tick,' and this risk has not been ruled out here.

No settler exists in this repo for RANKLIST/NFLFANTASY-governed series (grep for RANKLIST/NFLFANTASY under src/ returns nothing outside the fee fixture); a pod built on this thesis would need a new settler mapping result/settlement_value_dollars -> WIN/LOSS following the golf scalar-partial-payout precedent (src/kalshi_golf_settler.py), which has not been written or tested for this family.

Purge risk compounds the evidence gap: even once this product does settle a regular-season game, the empty-markets-array purge pattern observed on the one historical event means post-settlement field verification may become impossible after a retention window, the same caveat CLAUDE.md documents for golf LIST endpoints on settled markets.

Structural mismatch with P-022's validated case: golf round-leader fields are populated with real strokes for every player who teed off, giving a clean, complete candidate set; a single NFL game's 'most fantasy points' contest may include players who leave with an injury, get benched, or score zero, producing a very different (harder to model without external box-score data) tail than golf's stroke distribution.

This card cannot rule out a repeat of op_20260801_001's exact failure mode -- a plausible-sounding mechanism riding on a product whose actual cadence and observed history do not support the volume the thesis needs.
rule_ambiguities: Whether ESPN Fantasy publishes ANY 'official tie-breaking methodology' for game-level (not season-level) fantasy point totals is UNCONFIRMED -- WebFetch could not reach ESPN's own pages (same blocker documented in research/integrity/op_20260801_001_integrity_2026-08-01.json). This card assumes, but does not verify, that no such methodology exists for a single-game leaderboard (as distinct from season awards/rankings, which do sometimes have one) -- an integrity reviewer must attempt to resolve this against ESPN's actual published rules before this thesis can be sized.

Whether KXNFLFANTASYMOST's identical-text NFLFANTASY.pdf being byte-for-byte the RANKLIST.pdf template (confirmed via two independent WebFetch reads of the live contract_terms_url returning the same RANKLIST rulebook text) is Kalshi genuinely reusing the generic RANKLIST rulebook for this product (consistent with the CLAUDE.md-documented GOLDENGLOBESNOM.pdf precedent of a mislabeled-but-real template reuse), versus an artifact of this scout's own tooling. This scout could not diff raw PDF bytes/hashes to rule out a WebFetch summarization anomaly -- the next reader should re-fetch and hash-compare rather than trust this transcript alone.

The RANKLIST clause's 'if a tie results in a ranking being skipped... a market on being #2 will resolve to No' provision is written for ranked-list products with multiple strike positions (1st, 2nd, 3rd...); it is unclear whether KXNFLFANTASYMOST lists only a single 'most points' market per player (binary #1-only, matching the KXRANKLISTFF* structure this scout was sent to correct away from) or multiple rank strikes per game. The purged event gives no market-level evidence either way -- must be captured live.

Position Accountability Level in RANKLIST.pdf is stated as $25,000 per strike per Member -- unclear whether Kalshi applies the same limit to this reused-template product or has set a sport-specific override; not verifiable without an active market.

close_time / settlement-timing behavior for this family is completely unobserved (the one historical event returned close_time: null, status: null, strike_date: null even at the event level) -- CLAUDE.md's general open-market close_time gotcha (real close only appears at actual close) may or may not apply identically here, and a live game's kickoff time is presumably a much cleaner external anchor than golf's ambiguous multi-day windows, but this has not been tested against a real open market of this series.
